summary:
MISSION CONTROL – Design. Launch. Fly.

Mission Control is an interactive, browser-based space mission design game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It transforms complex space mission planning into an engaging learning experience where players take the role of mission planners and spacecraft operators.

Players choose scientific objectives and destinations, assemble spacecraft using different instruments and subsystems, and balance critical constraints such as mass, power, budget, data capacity, orbit and communications. They then select a launch vehicle and ground station before operating their mission through a 12-month simulation.

Featuring four mission scenarios, solo and up-to-four-player gameplay, specialised crew roles, interactive minigames, random mission crises and post-mission performance analysis, Mission Control encourages scientific curiosity, teamwork and systems thinking through play.

Design. Launch. Fly. Experience the challenges of space exploration.
details:
MISSION CONTROL is designed as a self-contained educational simulation that demonstrates how different spacecraft subsystems interact throughout a space mission.

How it works: Players begin by selecting one or two scientific objectives, choosing a destination, crew size and difficulty. They then enter the spacecraft design phase, where they select instruments and subsystems while balancing mass, available funds, power generation and consumption, and data capacity.

After spacecraft assembly, players select a launch vehicle, orbit and ground communication network. The spacecraft then enters a 12-month simulated mission featuring interactive activities such as science data collection, spectrum identification, communication and data transmission, power balancing, power routing and meteor defense. Random mission events, system damage and repair decisions introduce additional challenges.

Key benefits and intended impact:

  • Makes space mission planning concepts interactive and easier to understand.
  • Demonstrates systems thinking through connected engineering constraints.
  • Encourages strategic decision-making, experimentation and problem-solving.
  • Supports individual learning and collaborative gameplay for teams of up to four players.
  • Allows players to compare and share spacecraft configurations through design codes.

Technology used: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, HTML Canvas, Web Audio API and browser localStorage. The project is implemented as a self-contained browser application without requiring a backend or external JavaScript framework.

Creativity and design considerations: The project combines spacecraft design with interactive minigames, mission events, crew roles and post-mission analysis. It considers science objectives, spacecraft mass, power, budget, communication capacity, orbital choices, system reliability and mission risk.

The mission scenarios and engineering values are simplified for educational gameplay and are not intended to represent operational spacecraft specifications or real NASA mission predictions.
